name: Mark Wadsworth
role: Manager of the Bad Lands Cattle Co. (H. B. Wadsworth & Co.)
bio: Mark Wadsworth managed the Bad Lands Cattle Co., also listed as H. B. Wadsworth & Co., on the Little Missouri, and in May 1884 he waited in Medora for a thousand head of cattle coming from Minnesota. He reported only nominal winter losses in 1884–85 and over three thousand cattle on the range by March 1885, then went west to buy cow horses. In July 1885 he hired Rassie Deffebach as foreman, and that September the company shipped 309 beeves from Dickinson that the paper called the best lot shipped east from Dakota or Montana that year. In 1886 he experimented with grass seeds for a hay meadow, finding alfalfa and millet the most promising, though dry weather killed most of the millet.
